name: AGS neutral-kaon CP-violation experiment
notes: No collaboration record: a four-author Princeton group. No detector record (not assigned).

The Letter is titled "Evidence for the 2π decay of the K2 meson"; the 1980 Nobel citation calls the work "the discovery of violations of fundamental symmetry principles in the decay of neutral K-mesons", and BNL calls it a discovery.
BNL says the experiment began in 1963; the Letter was received on 10 July 1964 and published on 27 July 1964; the CERN Courier describes the 1964 publication.

physics_goals.quote: proposed using Brookhaven's AGS to verify a fundamental tenet of physics, known as CP symmetry, by showing that two different particles did not decay into the same products
physics_goals.value: Verify CP symmetry by showing that the long-lived neutral kaon never decays to two pions

summary.plain: Princeton physicists James Cronin and Val Fitch, with James Christenson and René Turlay, used Brookhaven's AGS to check that the long-lived neutral kaon never decays into two pions. It occasionally does, which broke the symmetry between matter and antimatter (CP).
summary.technical: Two-arm spark-chamber spectrometer with Cherenkov and scintillation triggers in a neutral beam at 30 degrees to 30 GeV protons on an internal Be target; K_L decays in helium gas were analysed for two-body π⁺π⁻ decay, which a CP-conserving world would forbid; the result was a branching fraction of about 0.2%.

unique_capabilities.quote: The introduction of spark chambers as charged particle detectors permitted precise track position determination, but also the chambers could be selectively triggered on appropriate classes of events.
unique_capabilities.value: Spark chambers that could be selectively triggered and gave precise track positions
